# Libraries and globals

Global tables reached by name. Their functions are camelCase, because a
library is a namespace and not an object (ADR 0034).

## task

The scheduler, and the only way a script asks for time. Timers run on the SimClock rather than the wall clock, so `task.wait(1)` is exactly 60 ticks at the default timestep on every machine and every run -- which is what makes a recorded replay reproduce (ADR 0025) and why there is no `tick()`.

## task — functions

### `cancel(thread: thread)`

Cancels a pending resumption -- a queued `task.defer` entry counts as one, so cancelling the thread `defer` returned stops its callback from running. A finished thread, an already-cancelled one and the running one all raise `script.err.task_not_scheduled`: none holds a pending resumption, and a pending resumption is the only thing this can take away.

### `defer(fn: (T...) -> (), arguments: T...): thread`

Enqueues `fn` on the deferred queue, so it runs at the next resumption point ordered against signal fires by when it was raised (§3.1). Returns the thread it will resume, which is the handle `task.cancel` takes.

### `delay(duration: number, fn: (T...) -> (), arguments: T...): thread`

Resumes `fn` at the first task-resume phase at or after `duration` seconds of SimClock time. Zero and negative durations both mean the next tick: `delay` must not run before it returns, so "at or after 0 seconds" cannot be satisfied by the phase you are standing in.

### `spawn(fn: (T...) -> (), arguments: T...): thread`

Resumes `fn` on a new coroutine **immediately**, synchronously, before returning -- the one non-deferred call in the library and deliberately so. Returns that thread. An error inside it is contained and does not propagate to the caller (§3.1).

### `wait(duration: number? = nil): number`

**Yields.** The calling thread parks until it completes.

Yields, and resumes at the first task-resume phase at or after `duration` seconds of SimClock time, defaulting to the next tick. Returns the elapsed sim time, which is a whole number of ticks times the timestep and therefore at least `duration`. Parks without an `Async` suffix because the name already says it waits (§9).

## Globals

### `warn(values: ...any)`

Prints like `print` and differs from it in severity and in nothing else: tab-separated, `tostring` applied to each argument. It reaches `DebugService.MessageOut` at `Enum.LogLevel.Warning`, and its text passes through verbatim rather than through the message catalog -- R3 governs what the engine says, not what a game says.
